purpose: Source-verified, non-secret contracts for the 1.3 card-testing order reader and rules (FEATURE-PLAN.md items 1-3, contracts C3-C5), and the shared public reason-code catalogue. Every WooCommerce fact below was read from the tagged release named in sources; line numbers are per version. The checkout-protection facts (rate-limit option and route scope, checkout page detection, order-pay and saved-payment paths) are pinned separately in tests/fixtures/checkout-protection-contracts.json. Code, response schema and tests share the reason_codes catalogue; no raw source error text is ever a code or a reason.

woocommerce_floor.note: The toolkit's WC requires at least floor.

woocommerce_current.note: The version the current test environment pins. A newer stable is adopted only with a fresh source check of every file below.

order_signals.covers: saved customer IP storage and the default order-attribution source type, read only in card mode
order_signals.version_source: the WC_VERSION constant; its first major.minor.patch triple decides
order_signals.outside_range: both signals return supported=false with reason unsupported_source_version (never a guessed off or empty value); order counts are still read, as payment health reads them
order_signals.note: OrderAttributionController and OrderAttributionBlocksController are byte-identical between 10.9.0 and 11.3.1; OrderAttributionMeta differs only in the origin-label formatter (lines 347-373), not in the prefix, field list, source_type field or (none) handling. The order column maps and the meta read order below are unchanged at the cited lines.

third_party_protection.note: No captcha, fraud-rule or gateway-setting adapter is approved for 1.3. Any later adapter needs its own lead-approved source receipt (exact plugin versions, settings keys, hook and route coverage, passive reads). Unsupported protection stays explicit unknown and does not block the core-only first version.

orders.eligible: type shop_order only; refunds (shop_order_refund) excluded by type; statuses trash, draft and auto-draft ignored; checkout-draft counted only as checkout_draft
orders.cohort_time: creation time for every cohort (HPOS wc_orders.date_created_gmt, legacy posts.post_date_gmt, both UTC datetime); the SQL selects creation >= history start only, so an order created before the history and failed or retried later is not observed (disclosed blind spot)

customer_ip.duplicates: a column: one value per order

hpos.operational_join: wc_order_operational_data.order_id = wc_orders.id, UNIQUE KEY order_id (10.9.0 OrdersTableDataStore.php:3390, 11.3.1 :3690): no join multiplication; a missing row is unavailable (operational_data_missing), never a missing origin

meta.table: wc_orders_meta (id auto-increment, order_id, meta_key, meta_value); KEY order_id_meta_key_meta_value (10.9.0 OrdersTableDataStore.php:3399, 11.3.1 :3699)
meta.crud_read: CustomMetaDataStore::get_meta_data_for_object_ids() selects with no ORDER BY (10.9.0 and 11.3.1 CustomMetaDataStore.php:269, :283); WC_Data::get_meta() returns the first loaded row of the key (abstract-wc-data.php:431 in both). The CRUD order of duplicate rows is therefore whatever index MySQL uses, not a defined order: in the 11.3.1 test environment CRUD returned the second-inserted duplicate, consistent with the order_id_meta_key_meta_value index (value order).
meta.reader_precedence: lowest wc_orders_meta.id per order (contract C4), chosen in PHP from one bounded meta read per chunk (meta_key = default attribution key). The integration test compares single-row orders with CRUD and duplicate-row orders with the lowest-id row read directly, and reports how many CRUD reads differed. WooCommerce's own attribution code does not write a second source_type row for an order that already has attribution (OrderAttributionController.php:163-166).

legacy.read: posts.post_date_gmt and post_status for shop_order posts, plus postmeta rows of the keys below for the candidate batch only
legacy.crud_read: read_order_data() reads get_post_meta( $id ) (class-wc-order-data-store-cpt.php:131 in both) and takes [0] of each key: _date_paid then _paid_date (:134, :141), _payment_method (:169), _customer_ip_address (:172), _created_via (:174); WordPress loads post meta ORDER BY meta_id, so [0] is the lowest meta_id. Non-internal meta (attribution) loads through WC_Data_Store_WP::read_meta() ORDER BY meta_id (class-wc-data-store-wp.php:83-92 in both) and get_meta() returns the first (abstract-wc-data.php:431).
legacy.reader_precedence: lowest meta_id per key in PHP, through both access paths (primary-key span or post_id probes), as payment health
legacy.paid_precedence: _date_paid (UTC Unix seconds) when its first row is truthy, else _paid_date (site-local Y-m-d H:i:s); PaymentRules::legacy_paid()

origin.missing: NULL or empty created_via; a separate missing_origin scope, never inferred
origin.other: any other value (admin, imports, renewals, POS and custom text): contextual counts only, the raw text is never kept

classes.accepted: valid paid date, or status processing, completed or on-hold (on-hold is never called paid)
classes.failed_unpaid: status failed and no valid paid date
classes.cancelled_unpaid: status cancelled and no valid paid date
classes.pending_unpaid: status pending and no valid paid date
classes.checkout_draft: status checkout-draft, whatever paid evidence it carries (paid evidence on a draft is a coverage anomaly: draft_paid_anomaly)
classes.other_status: anything else without a valid paid date (for example refunded unpaid or a custom status)
classes.invalid: creation NULL, malformed or at or after now, or a malformed or future paid date on a non-draft: excluded, its scope partial (invalid_timestamps)
classes.precedence: a valid paid date wins over a later failed or cancelled status

ip.source: the saved order customer IP, set at checkout from WC_Geolocation::get_ip_address() (classic includes/class-wc-checkout.php 10.9.0:453, 11.3.1:482; Store API OrderController.php 10.9.0:117, 11.3.1:140), which prefers X-Real-IP, then the first X-Forwarded-For entry, then REMOTE_ADDR (includes/class-wc-geolocation.php:82-95 in both): proxies and forwarded headers can supply it
ip.bound: 100 bytes; SQL returns at most 101 characters so a longer value is flagged over-long, never truncated into a valid address
ip.validation: one literal address accepted by inet_pton; lists, ports, zone IDs, brackets, prefixes, whitespace, leading-zero IPv4 octets and non-scalar values are invalid
ip.grouping: IPv4-mapped IPv6 as IPv4; IPv4 /24; IPv6 /64
ip.privacy: only failed orders in the current window are grouped; the prefix is keyed with a fresh random 32-byte HMAC key per call and replaced by a per-call sequence number; raw IP, prefix, digest and key are never returned, cached, logged, used as a cache key or compared across calls; only counts and shares are published

attribution.field: source_type is a default tracking field (src/Internal/Traits/OrderAttributionMeta.php:29 in both)
attribution.prefix: meta key is '_' + prefix + field; the prefix defaults to 'wc_order_attribution_' through the filter wc_order_attribution_tracking_field_prefix (OrderAttributionMeta.php:114-123 in both); the field list is filterable through wc_order_attribution_tracking_fields (:96). Either filter registered: the signal is unassessed (attribution_override_present), never missing-attribution evidence.
attribution.saved_when: the order_attribution feature is enabled (OrderAttributionController.php:111), on woocommerce_order_save_attribution_data from classic checkout (:179) or the Store API extension woocommerce/order-attribution (OrderAttributionBlocksController.php:93-121); values '(none)' are not saved (OrderAttributionMeta.php:251) and nothing is saved when every value is empty (OrderAttributionController.php:469-478); admin-created orders get source_type admin (:246)
attribution.feature_option: woocommerce_feature_order_attribution_enabled; enabled_by_default true (FeaturesController.php 10.9.0:347-353, 11.3.1:406-412); read as 'yes' === get_option( name, default ) (10.9.0:916, 11.3.1:972). Absent option inside the supported range: the source default (on). Any value other than yes: off (attribution_feature_disabled).

classes.unsupported: any other or over-64-byte value; it invalidates the comparison (attribution_value_unsupported)

attribution.bound: 64 bytes; SQL returns at most 65 characters
attribution.not_read: every other attribution field (source, referrer, UTM values, session data, user agent, device type)
attribution.consent: missing attribution can come from consent or tracking settings and is never independently suspicious; a feature switched on now does not prove it was on historically, so the comparison needs a populated baseline (at least 50% present over at least 100 baseline orders)

rules.note: Screening heuristics, not calibrated probabilities. No merchant setting or filter changes them in 1.3.

bounds.sentinel: row reads fetch one sentinel row past the chunk; metadata reads fetch one sentinel row past the per-batch and per-call bound and fold none of a batch that exceeds it

reason_codes_note: Lane core's codes are below (owner core), followed by the log summary codes (owner logs, PaymentErrors), the checkout protection codes (owner protection, CheckoutProtection) and the card-testing ability's own display and evidence limitation codes (owner ability, CardTesting). Every text is the exact PHP text; no code may carry raw source error text.

attribution_baseline_insufficient.text: Too few earlier orders recorded a marketing source to compare with, so missing marketing sources were not used as a sign.

attribution_feature_disabled.text: WooCommerce Order Attribution is switched off, so the marketing source sign was not checked. Missing marketing sources are not treated as suspicious.

attribution_override_present.text: A plugin changes how WooCommerce records where orders came from, so the marketing source sign was not checked.

attribution_storage_unavailable.text: The store does not keep where orders came from in a place this check can read, so the marketing source sign was not checked.

attribution_value_unsupported.text: Some orders carry a marketing source value this check does not recognise, so the marketing source sign could not be compared.

baseline_incomplete.text: Not every order for this payment method could be read, so it could not be compared with earlier orders.

baseline_insufficient_span.text: Earlier accepted or failed orders cover less than 7 days, too short to compare with, so only very large bursts can be detected.

baseline_insufficient_volume.text: Fewer than 100 accepted or failed orders were created before this window in the last 28 days, too few to compare with, so only very large bursts can be detected.

bucket_cell_cap.text: This check reached its limit for order times, so some hours could not be compared.

cause_unverified.text: This check reads order records only. It cannot confirm who or what caused failed orders, and it never checks the payment provider's records.

draft_paid_anomaly.text: Some unfinished checkout orders carry a payment date, which is unexpected, so counts for their payment method are incomplete.

empty_store.text: No orders were created in the last 28 days, so there is nothing to assess.

failed_order_volume_context.about: A fully observed burst whose failed share is below 50%: ordinary declines during busy trading, volume context only.

invalid_timestamps.text: Some orders have a future or malformed date and were left out, so counts for their payment method are incomplete.

ip_storage_unavailable.text: The store does not keep the network details of orders where this check can read them, so network concentration was not checked.

likely_card_testing.about: A burst with a failed share of at least 80%, network concentration and a marketing-source shift on complete core evidence, verified origin, instant method.

logs_unavailable.text: The payment plugin's logs could not be fully checked, so no all-clear can be given.

low_history.text: At least one payment method has too little earlier order history to compare with, so only bursts of 100 or more failed orders in one hour can be detected for it.

method_cap.text: More payment methods appeared on orders than this check tracks, so some orders were counted but not assessed.

method_kind_unknown.text: How this payment method takes payments is not verified, so its failed orders are shown as counts only, without a card-testing verdict.

method_manual.text: A manual payment method (paid outside checkout), so card testing does not apply.

method_test_mode.text: This payment method is in test mode, so its orders are not real customer payments and are not assessed.

missing_origin_orders.text: Some orders have no record of where they came from. They are assessed separately and can at most be a possible sign of card testing.

network_bucket_cell_cap.text: There were more recorded networks than this check compares at once, so network concentration could not be checked for some hours.

network_cap.text: There were more recorded networks than this check compares at once, so network concentration could not be checked for some hours.

no_applicable_scope.text: No payment method that charges at checkout had orders that could be assessed.

no_failed_orders.text: No failed orders were created in this hour, so there is nothing to compare.

operational_data_missing.text: Some orders are missing WooCommerce's order details record, so order activity could not be checked.

order_scan_budget.text: This check reached its order reading limit before reading every order in the last 28 days, so counts are lower bounds and no all-clear can be given.

order_state_basis.text: Counts are orders created in the window and still in that state when checked. Orders that later failed, were paid or were deleted are counted by their state now.

orders_unavailable.text: Orders could not be read from the store's order records, so card testing could not be checked.

origin_unverified.text: These orders have no record of where they came from, so whether they came through the checkout could not be established.

other_origin_orders.text: Some orders were created another way, for example by an administrator, an import or a subscription renewal. They are counted but not assessed.

possible_card_testing.about: A burst missing at least one likely requirement with a failed share of at least 50%, or an absolute lower-bound burst on a partial scan with the share unknown; missing-origin bursts at most reach this.

read_failed.text: Orders could not be read from the store's order records, so card testing could not be checked.

reader_mismatch.text: The order counts did not match the time window of this check, so they were not used.

recorded_network_limits.text: Recorded networks group the network details saved on orders. Offices, mobile carriers and proxies put many shoppers in one network, and card testers can spread over many, so networks are only supporting evidence.

row_cap.text: This check reached its order reading limit before reading every order in the last 28 days, so counts are lower bounds and no all-clear can be given.

share_unknown.text: Not every order was read, so the share of orders that failed is unknown.

tables_missing.text: Orders could not be read from the store's order records, so card testing could not be checked.

test_mode_unknown.text: Whether this payment method is in test mode could not be read, so test orders may be included.

unassessed_method_failed_orders.about: An hour with at least 20 failed orders on a payment method whose settlement kind is not verified: counts and investigation advice only.

unassigned_method_orders.text: Some orders have no payment method recorded. They are counted but not assessed.

unsaved_and_retried_orders.text: Older orders retried now, payment requests that failed without saving an order, and deleted orders are not measured by these counts.

unsupported_data_store.text: Orders could not be read from the store's order records, so card testing could not be checked.

unsupported_source_version.text: This WooCommerce version has not been verified for reading saved network and marketing source details, so those signs were not checked.

assessments_display_cap.text: More payment methods were assessed than are listed here, so only the strongest results are shown. The verdict and these limitations cover every assessment.

attribution_disabled.text: WooCommerce order attribution is off, so where orders came from is not recorded.

attribution_evidence_only.text: Order attribution records where orders came from. Keeping it on improves the evidence this check can use; it does not block bots or protect any checkout path.

attribution_fields_override.text: A plugin or theme changes which order attribution details are recorded, so they could not be read.

attribution_prefix_override.text: A plugin or theme changes how order attribution is stored, so it could not be read.

attribution_setting_unrecognised.text: The order attribution setting has an unexpected saved value, so whether it is on is not known.

byte_cap.text: Only part of the logs was read (size limit reached), so some errors may not have been counted.

checkout_page_invalid_setting.text: The saved checkout page setting is not a valid page.

checkout_page_missing.text: The checkout page set in WooCommerce no longer exists.

checkout_page_mixed.text: The checkout page contains both the checkout block and the classic checkout shortcode, so which one shoppers use is not known.

checkout_page_no_marker.text: The checkout page has no standard checkout block or shortcode, so a page builder, pattern or theme template may supply the checkout.

checkout_page_not_set.text: No checkout page is set in WooCommerce.

checkout_page_oversize.text: The checkout page is too large for this check to read.

checkout_page_unpublished.text: The checkout page set in WooCommerce is not published.

checkout_page_unreadable.text: The checkout page could not be read.

checkout_shortcode_renamed.text: A plugin or theme renames WooCommerce's checkout shortcode, so a classic checkout could not be recognised.

decline_detection_unsupported.text: Payment plugin logs are checked for errors only. Declined cards are not read from the logs in this version, so logged errors point to a possible payment fault, not to card testing.

diagnostics_denied.text: Not checked: your role is not allowed to see store diagnostics. A store administrator can check the payment plugin's logs.

episodes_display_cap.text: More suspicious hours were found than are listed, so only the strongest are shown for each payment method. Hours overlap, so their counts are never added together.

examples_changed.text: Some example orders changed or were deleted after they were counted, so they are not listed. The counts were not changed.

examples_display_cap.text: Only a few example failed orders are listed. They are orders to look at, not the full count.

file_cap.text: There were more log files than this check reads at once, so some errors may not have been counted.

file_unreadable.text: A payment plugin log could not be read, so some errors may not have been counted.

findings_display_cap.text: There were more findings than are listed here, so only the most important are shown. The verdict covers all of them.

log_directory_unavailable.text: The WooCommerce log folder could not be read, so payment plugin errors were not checked.

log_family_unknown.text: Some payment methods on these orders are not linked to a payment plugin whose logs this check can read, so their logs were not checked. This does not mean they logged no errors.

log_row_cap.text: The payment plugin's log had more recent entries than this check reads at once, so some errors may not have been counted.

logging_disabled.text: WooCommerce logging is switched off, so payment plugin errors were not checked.

logging_threshold_above_error.text: WooCommerce logging is set to skip ordinary errors, so payment plugin errors were not checked.

logging_unavailable.text: WooCommerce logging could not be read, so payment plugin errors were not checked.

method_facts_unavailable.text: The payment method settings could not be read, so no payment method could be assessed for card testing.

no_matching_log_source.text: No log from this payment plugin was found for this window, so its errors were not checked.

no_readable_protection.text: No setting this check can read covers this path.

no_supported_log_mapping.text: This payment plugin's logs are not supported yet, so they were not checked. This does not mean it logged no errors.

protection_enforcement_unverified.text: This check reads settings and the checkout page only. It cannot confirm that any protection works, and it cannot see protection added by other plugins, the server, a CDN or the payment provider.

rate_limit_checkout_off.text: WooCommerce's Rate limit Checkout setting is off. This does not mean nothing else protects this path.

rate_limit_filter_present.text: A plugin or theme changes Store API rate limits, so the limits in use are not known.

rate_limit_scope_unverified.text: Which request addresses Rate limit Checkout matches was not checked for this WooCommerce version.

rate_limit_setting_unrecognised.text: Rate limit Checkout has an unexpected saved value, so whether it is on is not known.

shared_log_source.text: This payment plugin's log is also linked to another payment plugin, so its errors could not be told apart and were not counted.

source_read_failed.text: The payment plugin's log could not be read.

stale_retention.text: WooCommerce keeps logs for less time than this window, so older errors may be missing from the count.

unparsed_entries.text: Some log entries were not in a format this check can read, so some errors may not have been counted.

unsupported_log_handler.text: WooCommerce saves its logs in a way this check cannot read, so payment plugin errors were not checked.

wc_version_unverified.text: This WooCommerce version has not been checked by this tool, so its checkout routes and settings are not described.
